(31669) 1999 JT
6
is an
Earth-crossing asteroid
belonging to the
Apollo
family of
asteroids
which also crosses the orbit of
Mars
.  1999 JT6 is the asteroid's
temporary discovery name
.  It has now been assigned a permanent number from the
Minor Planet Center
(31669) indicating that its orbit has been confirmed, but has not (at least so far) been assigned a name.  Only a small fraction of asteroids have been named.
It has an Earth
minimum orbit intersection distance
of 0.00354
AU
(328,978 miles), which is close enough to classify it as a
potentially hazardous asteroid
(PHA).  It will make a close approach to Earth on 14 December 2076 at 0.0260 AU (2,506,321 miles) and an even closer approach to the
minor planet
Ceres
on 16 Feb 2084 at 0.0171 AU (1,587,064 miles).
